_comment: Worked flagd definitions for every flag SPACE reads. Defaults here reproduce the behaviour of an unconfigured deployment, so serving this file unchanged changes nothing. See ../README.md for the subject shape and targeting attributes each flag expects. Guarded against drift by tests/flagd_reference.rs.

space-api-client-concurrency-quotas._comment: An empty object leaves every cap at its env/Helm value. Both fields are optional; an entry under `overrides` also allowlists that client id.

space-net-gateway-known-egress-domains._comment: The object form, not a bare array: OpenFeature resolves JSON as a structure, so no OpenFeature backend can return a top-level array. The inert default is {"domains": []} rather than the bare {} the other JSON flags use, because this flag's reader requires the key — an object without it is a malformed assignment and logs a warning on every gateway launch. flagd stringifies the nested array; the reader decodes it.

space-cluster-api-client-side-balancing._comment: Subjects arrive prefixed (`sandbox:`, `session:`, `org:`) and `cluster_id` is supplied as an attribute, so one definition can ramp a single cluster while leaving the rest on the Service client.

space-snapshot-retention-config._comment: Evaluated with the cluster id as the subject, so each cluster can be retuned on its own. Absent fields keep their env values; the sweeper validates the whole assignment before applying either field, and rejects one out of range rather than clamping it.
